items.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: Mitch was in the booth... 'I've got a conductor.' It was a split session... Norm Layton is going to be conducting for Don Cherry... So he says, 'Write yourself a couple of trombone parts.' ctx.x: Well you must have had an arrangement like with Columbia, did you get a percentage of the recording? Were you on contract?

Oh I started out like all the rest of the artists. The first break I got was through Mitch Miller. I met Mitch when I was writing for Harry James’ band, and he would come out to the west coast, and sit in the booth and oversee the sessions. And when I first went back to New York, this is let’s say five or six years later, after I’d been doing arranging for Harry James, I went back — I’d been on the west coast for a while and I decided gee I used to do, I was doing well, but I thought I could be doing better.
